name: One&Only Palmilla
positioning: Historic beachfront resort with hacienda-style architecture on the Baja Peninsula, overlooking the Sea of Cortez near San José del Cabo
best_for: Travelers who want a swimmable beach in Los Cabos
Guests drawn to Old Mexico character and history
Couples looking for spa time and ocean excursions
Travelers bringing a dog or cat

facts.text: The resort is set on the Baja Peninsula, overlooking the Sea of Cortez.
The resort has beachfront access to one of the region's few swimmable beaches.
In the 1950s Don Abelardo Rodriguez, son of the Mexican president, turned the site into a private home and eventually the region's first resort.
The resort has hacienda-style architecture and an old chapel.
Room furnishings include steel-studded wood doors and intricately carved wooden mirror frames.
The spa offers a temazcal experience, for which a shaman can be brought in.
Guests can surf right off the resort's beach.
Complimentary 10-minute foot massages are offered by the pool.
The hotel can arrange an overnight yacht charter for guests.
The resort is about a 10- to 12-minute drive from San José del Cabo, whose Thursday night art walks guests can join, and staff can curate gallery tours.
Suviche serves a Mexican-Japanese menu, and Seared is another of the resort's dinner restaurants.
The resort is pet-friendly, offering pet-sitting, dog walking and special pet supplies.

highlights.text: The resort has beachfront access to one of the region's few swimmable beaches, overlooking the Sea of Cortez.

The hotel can organize marine life and snorkeling excursions to Cabo Pulmo.

considerations.text: All payments must be made by credit card; the resort does not accept cash.
Los Cabos International Airport is 17 miles away, about a 20-minute drive.
